purpose: Give a native client one pre-authentication, non-secret, cacheable document that answers what it must know before authorization or feature routing: installation identity, exact allowed origins, compatibility versions and contract digest, supported authorization profiles, the site header rule, pre-authentication limits and the supported client contract window. The audited core serves an API identity document at GET /api/v1; this proposal extends that observed pattern with the fields a native application needs, without disclosing sites, policies or any authenticated metadata.

proposed_resources.purpose: Serves the closed discovery document with a strong ETag; the document is identical for every anonymous caller and never varies by credential.

security_invariants: The document is non-secret and identical for every anonymous caller; it never lists sites, organizations, workspaces, users, policies or installed extensions.
Allowed origins are exact HTTPS origins; a client refuses to send credentials to an origin outside the list.
The support URL is display-only, opened in an external user agent, and never receives native credentials or tokens.
Advertised authorization profiles constrain which flows a client may attempt; an unlisted flow is not attempted as a fallback.
A client outside the advertised client-contract window refuses mutations before sending them rather than degrading silently.
The document cannot grant capability: every advertised capability is re-checked by server authorization on use.
